builder_plan.scenario: Start with one repeated product task that has a measurable failure or cost.
builder_plan.change: Read the methods and identify one change you can isolate in that workflow.
builder_plan.baseline: Your current implementation on the same held-out tasks.
steps: Locate the paper's implementation and check its license, model support, data needs, and hardware requirements. Stop here if you cannot obtain the required artifacts.
Save a small set of representative product tasks and expected outcomes. Keep evaluation tasks out of any training or tuning, and choose quality and cost limits before running.
Run the baseline and the proposed change on identical inputs. Keep other settings fixed and repeat paired runs to expose variation.
Save per-task outputs, failures, timings, and all usage costs. Review regressions before expanding the test.
builder_plan.measure: Successful outcomes, response time, human rework, and total cost per successful task.
builder_plan.decision: Keep the change only if it meets your preselected quality and latency limits and improves the metric you care about after setup and operating costs. Otherwise retain the baseline. This is an exploration plan, not a validated recommendation.

title: CARROT: Competitive Adaptive Graph Clustering via Semi-Relaxed Optimal Transport
summary: CARROT replaces deep graph clustering pipelines that require a pre-specified cluster count K and implicitly favor balanced partitions, using semi-relaxed optimal transport with adaptive cluster capacities, a competition loss, and hard prototype pruning. The cost is a two-stage pipeline (embedding pre-training followed by joint embedding-assignment optimization) with added implementation complexity and hyperparameters governing competition and pruning. It can fail if the pre-trained embedding space is uninformative for the target graph, if the competition mechanism prunes genuine minority clusters rather than degenerate ones, or if benchmark gains on five public datasets do not transfer to noisier production graphs.
rationale: This addresses unsupervised attributed graph clustering rather than LLM inference or training, so it matters only if the reader's production workloads include graph-structured data, in which case a single-GPU evaluation on their own graphs is warranted before adoption.

claims.statement: CARROT replaces deep graph clustering pipelines that require a pre-specified cluster count K and implicitly favor balanced partitions, using semi-relaxed optimal transport with adaptive cluster capacities, a competition loss, and hard prototype pruning. The cost is a two-stage pipeline (embedding pre-training followed by joint embedding-assignment optimization) with added implementation complexity and hyperparameters governing competition and pruning. It can fail if the pre-trained embedding space is uninformative for the target graph, if the competition mechanism prunes genuine minority clusters rather than degenerate ones, or if benchmark gains on five public datasets do not transfer to noisier production graphs.

Claims state-of-the-art NMI and ARI on five public attributed-graph benchmarks, with accurate unsupervised recovery of the cluster count K and preservation of size-imbalanced communities; no multiplicative factor is reported.
